evidence.note: Enters plan mode, writes halyard-plan.md, resolves tech-stack/concurrency decisions before coding — genuine upfront decomposition rather than an undifferentiated stream.

TaskCreate markers segment the work into discrete milestones sequenced by dependency: foundation/db → SigV4 auth → admin API → S3 CRUD. Storage substrate and auth (highest-uncertainty foundations) come first.

Later milestones (notifications, lifecycle, console, conditional requests) are each treated as discrete units in a reasonable dependency order; the browser-graded console is scoped as its own track (step 73/110-118) — an anchor-8 trait.

Verification is only a late curl /_health check, not a per-milestone acceptance gate. No milestone has a stated 'done' check (e.g. boto3 round-trip) before the next is layered on, so the risky foundations are built early but never proven early.

reasoning: The agent clearly decomposed the build into an ordered hierarchy of subsystems via repeated TaskCreate milestones with a defensible dependency order (storage substrate and SigV4 auth first, dependent features after), and scoped the console as a separate grading track — exceeding anchor 5 and touching anchor 8. However it lacks the defining anchor-8 trait of a stated acceptance/'done' check per milestone: verification is deferred to the end rather than gating each layer, and the high-uncertainty foundations are sequenced early but never proven early. This places the behavior between anchors 5 and 8, at a 6.
